Since \(y=\prod_{j=0}^{21}\cos(4j+2)^\circ=\prod_{m=1}^{22}\sin(4m^\circ)=\prod_{m=1}^{22}\sin\frac{m\pi}{45}\),  
the identity \(\prod_{m=1}^{(N-1)/2}\sin\frac{m\pi}{N}=\frac{\sqrt N}{2^{(N-1)/2}}\) with \(N=45\) gives
\[
y=\frac{\sqrt{45}}{2^{22}}.
\]
Also
\[
x=\prod_{k=1}^{89}\cos k^\circ=\prod_{k=1}^{89}\sin k^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{90}}{2^{89}}.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{y}{x}=\frac{\sqrt{45}/2^{22}}{\sqrt{90}/2^{89}}
=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}2^{67}=2^{133/2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac27\log_2 \frac{y}{x}=\frac27\cdot \frac{133}{2}=19.
\]

\boxed{19}
